cases.description: When the JsonSchema instance has a non‑null TypeValidator (e.g., created from a schema that defines a "type" keyword), hasTypeValidator() should return true.
When the JsonSchema instance has no TypeValidator (e.g., created from a schema without a "type" keyword), hasTypeValidator() should return false.
Calling hasTypeValidator() should never throw an exception regardless of the internal state of the schema.
A schema that defines a top‑level "type": "object" should cause hasTypeValidator() to return true.
When the "type" keyword is an array of allowed types, the schema still has a TypeValidator, so hasTypeValidator() returns true.
A schema that only contains an "anyOf" with sub‑schemas that have types but no top‑level "type" keyword should return false.
A schema that $ref‑s to another definition which defines a "type" should resolve the reference and report true.
A $ref that points to a schema without a top‑level "type" keyword should result in false.
A schema that only defines an "enum" (no "type") must return false.
Even after calling initializeValidators() on a schema that lacks a top‑level "type", hasTypeValidator() remains false.
After initializeValidators() on a schema that already has a top‑level "type", the method still returns true.
A schema where "type" is explicitly set to null should not create a TypeValidator and therefore returns false (no exception should be thrown).
When the "type" keyword is a number (invalid type definition), getTypeValidator() should throw IllegalArgumentException, causing hasTypeValidator() to propagate the exception.
A $ref that points to a non‑existent definition should cause schema resolution to fail and throw a JsonSchemaException when hasTypeValidator() accesses the TypeValidator.
A schema that references itself directly creates a circular reference; attempting to resolve the TypeValidator should eventually overflow the stack.
If the root schema node is null (e.g., schema parsing returned null), calling hasTypeValidator() should result in a NullPointerException when getTypeValidator() dereferences the node.
When the "type" array contains a non‑string element (the number 5), the TypeValidator creation should fail with IllegalArgumentException.
If the implementation does not allow a top‑level "type" together with "anyOf" (or similar combinators) for TypeValidator creation, it may throw UnsupportedOperationException.
